title: feat(objectql): a nested-relation condition on a read verb is one read-scoped in-database subquery per relationship, up to three, where it is provably the same read as the id read
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-elon-musk"} -->
_Requested by **Elon** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01WedDzV26nniwxv7jC88B9D?thread=cmsg_01WedDzV26nniwxv7jC88B9DWLrF6ZURGN6BVpSbuDyHTg)_

Part of #33626 — the engine and analytics halves land here; the card stays open until #33876 lands maintainer ruling Q2 (the engine's `INVALID_FILTER` / 400 for MongoDB / OData, with the ADR-0139 capability bit). The other parts are their own follow-up cards citing #33626 and its rulings: #33875 (skills text, Tier H), #33876 (above, Tier H), #33877 (multi-valued relation as a JSON-membership semi-join), #33878 (a dataset measure's own `filter`).

Clause-②: yes (widening) — `{ account: { status: { $ne: 'cancelled' } } }` on `find`, `findOne`, `count` and `aggregate` (and so every analytics face that hands the engine the nested form) is served whatever the number of matching related records on a driver that compiles the subquery (the SQL drivers; the in-memory driver evaluates it in process), where more than 1,000 answered `INVALID_FILTER` / 400. The related read is planned through its whole pipeline as the caller and its final `where` becomes the subquery's scope; related-object read restrictions the planned read observes are carried into the subquery, or the hop falls back to the id read (the related object read as the caller, then `$in`, under the 1,000 cap). A relation key inside the condition may now carry a condition of its own, down to ADR-0071's three relationships (`{ contact: { account: { region: { name: 'NA' } } } }`), where a second level answered `INVALID_FILTER` / 400; each hop is that object's own read, and a fourth relationship is refused by name. On the analytics engine-aggregate path a dotted `where` leaf through up to three relationships (`order.customer.tier`), and a cross-object leaf in a compiled dataset's own definition-level `filter`, reach the engine as that nested condition, where both answered `INVALID_FIELD` / 400. Still the id read, under the 1,000 cap: a related object on another datasource, a federated related object, a driver that compiles no subquery (MongoDB, OData), a related object an object-scoped middleware or an `afterFind` hook shapes, a related object read under different driver options than the outer object (decided before planning where the registry answers it: the two objects' tenancy class under a walled posture), a related read that a middleware answers itself, a multi-valued relation and the `update` / `delete` verbs. A hop that falls back after planning dispatches the related read twice: its middleware chain and `beforeFind` hooks run for the planned read and again for the id read. A per-measure `filter` carrying a cross-object leaf stays refused. The SQL echo of a dataset `filter` carrying a served cross-object leaf refuses `INVALID_FILTER` / 400 where it refused `INVALID_FIELD` / 400; neither printed a statement.
Metadata-protocol: added — a compiled dataset's definition-level `filter` (`@objectstack/service-analytics`) now accepts a cross-object leaf on the engine-aggregate path, where it answered `INVALID_FIELD` / 400: a new accepted value for a dataset author.
Skills-docs: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/query-syntax.mdx` and `content/docs/kernel/contracts/data-engine.mdx` describe the subquery, the three-relationship limit, where the id read and its cap still apply and which drivers compile the subquery. `skills/objectstack-query` still says "up to 1000 related ids" and one level for every relation; that is now stricter than the engine for a single-valued relation on a read verb (a follow-up skills-only change, governed).

Area-lease pilot #33059, area A3. Contract record 6898853007 (PASS on `96c23127`, no must-fix) is answered on this head: S2–S5 and N2 below. The L2 record 6900638852 (PASS on `2d2eaa73`) is answered too: S1 by the seat's option C (the author-facing rule on both docs pages, the planned-leaf docblock), S2 by this body, S3 by the seat's rulings (Acceptance notes), N2 in the pin.

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么：在上一版「只在可证明等同时走库内子查询」的基础上，把注册表能直接判定的回退提前到规划之前：关联对象是联邦对象（external），或在有组织墙的租户姿态下两个对象的租户类别不同，直接走 id 读取，关联读取只执行一次；changeset 与两篇文档列全了所有仍走 id 读取（及 1000 上限）的情形，并写明：在驱动调用之后收窄关联对象行的读规则，只有注册在该对象上（对象级中间件或 afterFind 钩子）才约束关系条件。本轮合并 main，解决与 #33897（View All 读者丢弃必填主表的父链）在 `engine-readable-ids-permission-formula.ts` 的冲突：两者都保留，先执行 View All 丢弃，再只对丢弃后仍保留的关系条件叶子做 id 预读；调用者写在必填主表上的关系条件永不随主表自身的读取范围一起被丢弃。
- 为什么改：合同评审 6898853007 指出联邦关联对象的子查询不能证明等同、回退时关联对象的中间件与 beforeFind 钩子会执行两次、驱动选项比较只钉了一个方向、文档漏列两种回退情形。
- 风险与回滚：所有改动都只把更多情形导向 main 原有的 id 读取（更保守）；规划后才能判定的回退（中间件自行应答、只有本次请求决定的驱动选项差异）仍会二次执行，已在文档与 changeset 声明并钉住次数。冲突解决改变了两项改动交汇处的行为，属于已解决的冲突，需补 delta L1 与 L2 评审。回滚即 revert 本 PR。
- 先看：`packages/objectql/src/engine-readable-ids-permission-formula.ts`（`composeReadableIdsChain` 末尾：View All 丢弃与关系条件叶子的交汇）、`packages/objectql/src/relation-semi-join.ts`（`relationSemiJoinServes` 的两条规划前判定）、`packages/rest/src/data-nested-object-door.test.ts`（真实 SQLite / PG 上两个方向的驱动选项与租户类别钉子）。
- 两分钟验证：`pnpm --filter @objectstack/rest exec vitest run src/data-nested-object-door.test.ts`，预期全部通过（PG 单元需 `OS_TEST_POSTGRES_URL`，未设时跳过）。
- 需要你做的：无，席位落地（卡片保持打开，等 #33876；注册时声明的裁决见 #34155）。

## What changes

- **The registry-answered fallbacks are decided before planning** (`relationSemiJoinServes`), so the related read is dispatched once, as the id read: a federated related object (ADR-0015 `external`), and, under a posture that walls organizations, a related object of another tenancy class than the read's object (one tenant-scoped, the other platform-global or federated, `isDriverTenantScopedSchema` in `engine-driver-options.ts`, the one spelling `buildDriverOptions` also reads).
- **What is still decided after planning dispatches the related read twice**, declared in the changeset and both docs pages and pinned by count: a related read a middleware answers itself or adds rows to (after planning), and driver options that differ only by what the request records per object (at the executor boundary). Under the `single` posture two tenancy classes read under the same options and still compose (CONTROL).
- **The driver-options comparison is pinned in both directions on a real driver** (SQLite, PostgreSQL 16): the outer read unscoped with the related read scoped, and the opposite; and the tenancy-class decision in its other direction (a tenant-scoped read on a related object that is no tenant's), with the related read dispatched once.
- **Docs and changeset** list every case that keeps the id read and its 1,000 cap, adding the two missing ones (a related object read under different driver options than the read's own object, most commonly its tenant scope; a related read a middleware answers itself) and the federated related object.
- **The author-facing rule for after-driver read rules** is on both docs pages and in the `planRelationSemiJoinLeaf` docblock: a read rule that narrows a related object's rows after its driver call bounds a relation condition on that object only when it is registered for that object, as an object-keyed middleware or an `afterFind` hook (the bound ADR-0139 D5.2 sets for a `ReadableIds` parent).
- Behaviour on every other path is unchanged from `96c23127`.

## Acceptance notes

- **S1, by the seat's option C.** The author-facing rule is stated on both docs pages and in the `planRelationSemiJoinLeaf` docblock: a read rule that narrows a related object's rows after its driver call bounds a relation condition only when it is registered for that object (an object-keyed middleware or an `afterFind` hook), as ADR-0139 D5.2 bounds a `ReadableIds` parent. A registration-time declaration that would let the engine know such rules by another fact is #34155 (`needs-user-decision`: it widens the spec contracts surface).
- **A second dispatch on a fallback after planning.** A hop whose fallback is decided only after the related read was planned — a middleware answering the related read, or driver options only the request sets — runs the related object's middleware chain and `beforeFind` hooks twice (planned, then the id read), where main ran them once. Declared in the changeset and both docs pages; pinned as two dispatches (`engine-nested-relation-lowering.test.ts`), with one dispatch pinned for every registry-decided fallback.
- **Seat 6's commits taken.** Four commits from `claude/project-thread-m4k79t` (tip `39056411`) are cherry-picked with `-x`: `6e35a5e5` and `d599a82e` with their wording on one after-driver boundary left out (that boundary is S1, above), `6c7f6aef` and `39056411` unchanged. An earlier work-in-progress commit of this round (`777c4d06`) duplicated the first and is reverted on the branch (`dc2fd16a`), no history rewritten.
- **Where the 1,000 cap stays.** For a federated related object the cap stays, by the seat's ruling (S3 option A, area S2 thread): no driver prepares a remote object that appears only inside a subquery. For a single-valued hop across tenancy classes under an organization wall the cap stays at this head; serving it as a subquery carrying the related read's own driver options is #34157.
- **Conflict against #33897, resolved.** `origin/main` (`86350e12`) carried #33897 (`3c2fb325`, card #33696, ruling 6893666857), which conflicted with this branch in `packages/objectql/src/engine-readable-ids-permission-formula.ts` (the imports and `composeReadableIdsChain`'s tail). Both are kept: the View-All drop of a required master's leaf over unrestricted hops runs first; a leaf the nested-relation lowering planned is the caller's own condition on the master, never the master's read scope, so the drop never removes it (without that exclusion it would have dropped the caller's condition, pinned by the new interaction pin and its ablation); the planned-leaf id read runs only for leaves that survive the drop; the composition runs over the pruned tree. Both import sets are kept. `engine.ts` auto-merged, and its change from main is only the `_registry` accessor #33897 adds to the chain host. This is a resolved conflict, so delta L1 and L2 reviews are owed on `6062ec9c`.
- **N2 (title).** The title already qualifies the subquery as "where it is provably the same read as the id read" and carries no "no id cap" promise; it is unchanged.
- driver-memory serves the form in process (maintainer ruling Q1 on #33626, comment 6889549817).
- MongoDB / OData keep main's capped id read (no refusal); the ruled engine `INVALID_FILTER` / 400 and the ADR-0139 capability bit are #33876, which is why this PR is `Part of`. Until that bit exists the engine plans the subquery only for the drivers it names.
- `skills/objectstack-query` still teaches "up to 1000 related ids" and one level (governed, #33875).
- The echo of a dataset `filter` carrying a served cross-object leaf refuses `INVALID_FILTER` (it refused `INVALID_FIELD` before); both are 400 refusals of a statement that cannot be printed.
- The one hop-limit constant for objectql and service-analytics is not in this PR: `@objectstack/objectql` is only a devDependency of `@objectstack/service-analytics`, so sharing it needs a runtime dependency or a `@objectstack/spec` export; the two stay tied by their docblocks.
